title: Learning
note: This is the ruler learning the right books: on righteousness and statecraft, on elephants, horses, chariots and weapons. It sits among the chapters on rule, but it is spoken generally, because it benefits everyone.

couplets.plain: Learn what should be learned, and learn it without flaw. Once you have learned it, live up to it.
couplets.pm: Learn what is worth learning without flaw, then stand on the path it teaches. Worth learning means what teaches righteousness, wealth, pleasure and release, since other subjects are no use to people of short lives, many ills and small minds. Flawless learning clears error and doubt through long study with good people.

links.quote: Once you have learned it, live up to it
links.reason: Is not satisfied with study alone: what is learned must be lived up to.

couplets.plain: What they call numbers and what they call letters: these two, they say, are the eyes of those who live.
couplets.pm: The ignorant speak of numbers and of letters. Those who know call these two arts the eyes of those lives distinguished by greater understanding. Letters take in words too. They are eyes because they are the tools for seeing righteousness and the other aims of life.

links.quote: What they call numbers and what they call letters
these two, they say, are the eyes of those who live

couplets.plain: Those said to have eyes are the learned. The unlearned have two sores on their faces.
couplets.pm: Only the learned are praised as having eyes, because theirs is the eye of wisdom, which sees what is distant in place and time. The unlearned have two sores on their faces, for they have only eyes of flesh, which bring pain through disease and the like.

links.quote: Those said to have eyes are the learned
The unlearned have two sores on their faces
links.reason: Reduces the eyes of the unlearned to a pair of sores.
Sets working eyes against sores in the face to show what learning does for a person.

couplets.plain: To meet so that people are glad, and to part so that they long to meet again: that is the way of the learned.
couplets.pm: The way of the learned is to meet everyone so that they rejoice, and to leave so that they wonder how they can meet again. Seeing their good conduct and hearing their sweet, helpful words, everyone comes to feel loving-kindness for them.

links.quote: that is the way of the learned
links.reason: Describes the way of the learned among others, welcomed and then missed.

links.quote: to part so that they long to meet again

couplets.plain: Some learn, though it means yearning like the poor before the rich. Those who don’t learn are the lowest.
couplets.pm: Learning is good even at the cost of a humble stance. So those who learn, standing before their teachers as the poor stand before the rich, are the highest. Those too ashamed to do it are always the lowest. They lost true learning for a false sense of honour, and they never gain understanding.

links.quote: yearning like the poor before the rich
links.reason: Finds it worth the humbling of yearning like the poor before the rich.

links.quote: Those who don’t learn are the lowest
links.reason: Ranks those who don’t learn lowest of all.

links.quote: Some learn, though it means yearning
links.reason: Speaks of the one who learns, who may have to stoop like the poor before the rich.

couplets.plain: A well in the sand gives water as far as you dig. People’s understanding flows as far as they learn.
couplets.pm: A well in sand yields water in measure with the digging, and people’s understanding flows in measure with their learning. So don’t stop at a little: go on learning more. This holds where fate doesn’t oppose it, so it doesn’t clash with the earlier saying that inborn understanding wins out.

links.quote: People’s understanding flows as far as they learn
links.reason: Promises that understanding, like a well dug in sand, flows as far as you go.

couplets.plain: To the learned, every country is their country and every town their town. Why then does anyone go without learning until they die?
couplets.pm: For a learned person, any land and any town is as good as their own. So why do people pass their days unlearned until they die? Other lands and towns take such a person in as their own, with gifts and honour, so nothing is better than learning. Do it always. It says “until death” because learning goes on with the soul.

links.quote: To the learned, every country is their country
links.reason: Says of the learned alone that no town is foreign to them.

links.quote: Why then does anyone go without learning until they die

couplets.plain: What you learn in one birth shelters you for seven.
couplets.pm: The learning gained in one birth goes on to help you through seven. Like deeds, it stays in the soul and enters wherever the soul enters. Helping means guiding you onto the good path.

links.reason: Claims for learning a reward that outlives the body and serves through seven births.

couplets.plain: Seeing that the world delights in what delights them, the learned desire it all the more.
couplets.pm: The learned delight in learning, and seeing that the world delights in it too, they desire it all the more. They delight in tasting words and meanings, in renown, wealth and honour, and in the righteousness and release to come. The world delights in learning from them. Wealth brings trouble and enemies, so they want this instead.

links.quote: the world delights in what delights them
links.reason: Shows a delight that grows by being shared with the world.

links.quote: the learned desire it all the more
links.reason: Looks into the hearts of the learned to find why they keep at it.

couplets.plain: Learning is the great wealth that can’t be destroyed. All else is not wealth.
couplets.pm: The excellent wealth that can’t perish is learning. All the rest, such as gems and gold, is not wealth. It can’t perish because heirs, thieves, the strong and rulers can’t take it, and giving it to those who serve you doesn’t lessen it. It is excellent because it stays with the worthy.

links.reason: Holds it beyond destruction, where all else counts as no wealth at all.

links.quote: Learning is the great wealth that can’t be destroyed
links.reason: Applies the word wealth to learning and strips it from all else.
